Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark LoopArena for models acting as runtime Controllers of a fixed coding agent (Worker): Type I (160 four-way contract-selection questions), Type II (80 task slices), Type III (80 full tasks); 6 Controller models plus no-control and fixed-control reference policies compared

No SDD approach. Loop Engineering: Controller-Worker harness (outer loop: Controller model issues structured Loop Contracts; inner loop: Worker ReAct coding agent; temporary Reporter builds an Evidence Packet). Reference policies: no control (Worker runs autonomously) and fixed control (persistent-goal restatement inspired by Codex /goal). Version: Not stated (frozen run manifest; code at github.com/AMAP-ML/LoopArena)

Evidence Packet (Reporter's four fields: task_context_and_constraints, work_history_and_current_state, verification_and_evidence, open_issues_and_uncertainty, plus cited Worker turns and turn budget); Loop Contract (action advance/verify/stop, rationale, worker_instruction with goal, context, required_outcomes, prohibited_actions, completion_condition; protected_invariants; verification_acceptance_condition); task specification of the source benchmark

Bootstrap orientation segment (Worker, no implementation) -> control cycle repeated: Worker segment -> Reporter summarizes (read-only) -> harness formats Evidence Packet -> Controller issues Loop Contract (advance / verify / stop) -> harness renders next Worker instruction; stop submits workspace to the task evaluator. Ends on Controller stop, budget exhaustion or protocol failure

Tasks: 80 paired full tasks and slices from SCBench, BeyondSWE, LoopsBench, plus 160 Type I questions. Configurations: 6 Controller models; baselines no control and fixed control. Held constant: Worker (Qwen3.7-Plus) and Reporter model, tools, starting workspace, prompts, execution budget (600 Worker turns or 7,200 s; 128 control cycles), evaluator; Controller temperature 0 for open models, provider defaults for GPT-5.5 and Claude. Acceptance tests: source-native executable evaluators. Repetitions: K = 3 per task and policy (reference runs collected once and reused); Type I one response per question. Human intervention: none. Extra: Worker swapped to DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 20 tasks

Type III: GPT-5.5 best SSR 36.25% (vs fixed control 31.25%, no control 27.50%), range 24.17-36.25%; Type II: Claude Opus 4.8 best 58.75% (fixed control 55.00%). GLM 5.2 below both references. Cost: Controller-guided runs cost more than references; DeepSeek-V4-Flash cheapest Controller calls ($0.15) but highest Worker cost (total $32.66). Same SSR (33.75%) reached at $11.58 (Qwen3.6) vs $20.63 (Claude Opus 4.8). Type I: GPT-5.5 best (61.875%), all above shortcut baselines (max 30.625%). No significance tests of differences

Distinguished Controllers, though Type III differences are small (24-36%) and the best Controllers exceed fixed control by a few points. Type II ordering correlates with Type III (rho 0.7353; 2 of 13 strictly ordered pairs reverse) at 60.6% lower cost; rankings broadly stable across two Worker models (rho 0.80 / 0.74). Repeatability: 3 runs per task, many tasks with mixed 1/3 or 2/3 outcomes (Table 14); Type I answers confirmed by two replay schedules. Limitations stated: repository-level coding only, one Controller-Worker organization with structured handoffs; other domains, Worker families, multi-Worker settings not covered

Full-task loop control remains difficult (best 36.25%), leaving room for improvement; extension to other software domains, Worker families, multi-Worker settings and loop organizations, and beyond coding (needs domain-specific tasks and executable evaluators). Execution cost under a Controller's guidance can outweigh savings on Controller calls
